newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Dem. leader says will support prison bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Dem. leader says will support prison bonds.

text.p: Illinois House Democratic Leader Michael Madigan has changed his opposition to a state bonding program for corrections and will now support some debt issuance for prison construction, his spokesman said Friday.
Steve Brown said Madigan, D-Chicago, the minority leader in the House, changed his mind after meeting with state prison workers.
Madigan hoped that more prisons would ease overcrowding and allow prison officials to begin dealing with well-publicized problems of drug use and sex among prisoners, according to Brown.

Democratic opposition during the last two legislative sessions derailed Gov. Jim Edgar's plans to sell general obligation bonds to finance prisons. Even though the majority of lawmakers in both the House and Senate are Republicans like Edgar, Democratic votes were needed to reach a required three-fifths majority approval for new bonding authorization.

Unable to issue GO bonds for prisons, the state's Bureau of the Budget tapped into existing authorization to issue certificates of participation. However, a lawsuit filed earlier this year by a group of Democratic members of the Illinois House, forced the state to postpone a $85.6 million prison COPs issue.

State officials contended the lawsuit, which challenges the legality of $19.2 million of COPs sold through a lease-purchase agreement entered into by the Illinois Department of Central Mangement Service on behalf of the Illinois Department of Public Aid, made it impossible to issue any other COPs, including the ones for prisons.
Brown said the Edgar Administration had been trying to evade legislative approval through the issuance of COPs.

He added that Madigan, who is not a plaintiff in the COPs lawsuit, would still have to review any prison GO bonding plan Edgar may present to lawmakers either during their fall veto session in November or early next year in light of continued concerns over the state's fiscal condition.
Officials with Edgar Administration were not immediately available to comment on if or when the governor planned to resubmit a prison bonding plan to the General Assembly.
